newsitem.title: PANAMA: Service at Panama airport not 100 percent till '97.
newsitem.headline: Service at Panama airport not 100 percent till '97.

text.p: Traffic at Panama's Tocumen International Airport will not return to normal until the middle of next year following a crippling strike by air traffic controllers, a Civil Air Service spokesman said on Friday.
"We are currently operating at 80 percent and plan to be at 100 percent sometime in 1997," Victor de la Hoz told Reuters.
Foreign airlines partially resumed service on Thursday under a government contingency plan using air traffic controllers from the United States during peak international traffic hours.
De la Hoz said late night traffic at Tocumen would be added in January for a six-month period before returning to full 24-hour service by mid-1997.
"The strike is over. There are no plans to reintegrate the fired workers. What we're trying to do now is find a solution and re-establish a new system," he said.
The government dismissed at least 88 of 94 striking air traffic controllers who had stopped work on Tuesday demanding better pay and pension benefits.
Representatives of the dismissed air traffic controllers criticised the government for paying the replacement workers at least $200 more a month than what they earned on average.
The controllers walked out after talks broke down over the weekend on a payraise to $2,000 a month from an average of $600.
They also wanted a package allowing them to retire earlier than the national average of 62 years for men and 57 years for women.
